subject: Dedicated capacity commit - clarification on Capacity Units, discounts & SLA redlines
messages:
From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
To: Elena Torres <elena.torres@healthbridge.com>, procurement@healthbridge.com
Cc: neha.kapoor@redwood.com, marcus.lin@redwood.com

Subject: Dedicated capacity commit - initial proposal and attachments

Elena / HealthBridge procurement team,

Thanks again for the conversation this morning. Per request, attached is a concise proposal for Dedicated capacity pricing and a short SOW appendix that maps commit levels to reserved GPU pools. High-level highlights: 

- Commit tiers (monthly reserved "Capacity Units" or CUs): 100 CU, 300 CU, 900 CU.
- Discount schedule: applied to list price for Dedicated compute only; higher commits receive larger discounts (see attached spreadsheet).
- Burst policy: customers can burst above reserved CUs for up to 20% of monthly reserved capacity at a superset on-demand rate; bursts are billed separately.
- Throughput guidance & SLOs: we propose throughput baselines and p95 latency targets per CU in the contract appendix; service credits tied to monthly availability are specified in Appendix A.

Attachments: Redwood_Dedicated_Pricing_Proposal_v3.xlsx, SOW-Dedicated-Appendix.pdf

Next steps: if you can confirm which commit tier you're evaluating and the preferred contract term (12 or 36 months), I'll circulate a redline-ready snippet for the contract team and schedule a 30-min call to finalize.

Best,
Jordan Blake
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

From: Elena Torres <elena.torres@healthbridge.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>, procurement@healthbridge.com
Date: Tue, 14 Sep 2026 11:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity commit - initial proposal and attachments

Jordan, thanks for the proposal and the quick follow. A few clarifying questions from our side before we loop legal: 

1) Capacity Unit definition: the spreadsheet uses "CUs" but doesn't define hardware equivalence. Can you confirm what 1 CU maps to (GPU type, memory, or equivalent GPU-hours)? We need a deterministic definition we can reference in the contract.

2) Throughput guarantees: please provide the specific metric definition you expect to use in the SLA. Is it tokens/sec per CU, requests/sec, or something else? Also indicate context length assumptions and model family used for the baseline (we benchmark at 4k context).

3) Service credits: the appendix mentions credits but doesn't show how credits are calculated or any cap relative to monthly fees. We typically require a clear formula and a hard cap (e.g., not exceeding monthly fees or X% of fees).

4) Commit vs. usage: If our usage spikes above the commit for a given month, how are overage charges applied and do overages impact the discount tier on a go-forward basis?

5) Discount cadence: does the discount apply immediately on invoice once the commit is signed, or is there a ramp (e.g., month 1 at 50% discount of final level, full discount after 3 months)?

Please reply with suggested contract phrasing for the Capacity Unit definition and the SLA/service credit clause. If easier, we can take a short call tomorrow afternoon.

Regards,
Elena Torres
Head of Procurement (HealthBridge)
elena.torres@healthbridge.com

From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
To: karthik.iyer@redwood.com, neha.kapoor@redwood.com, marcus.lin@redwood.com
Date: Wed, 15 Sep 2026 08:30:00 -0700
Subject: Fwd: HealthBridge questions - draft redlines for Capacity Unit + SLA wording

Team — forwarding HealthBridge's questions. I'm proposing the draft language below to put into the SPA/SOW redlines. Please review and flag any legal/ops concerns. If we can sign off internally I will send to Elena with a tracked redline.

Proposed definitions & clauses (draft):

1) "Capacity Unit (CU)" - means one (1) capacity unit equivalent to one (1) GPU-Equivalent Hour on an NVIDIA Ampere A100-80GB baseline (or a commercially available model variant providing comparable throughput and memory characteristics), measured under Redwood's standard benchmarking configuration (4,096 token context, float16 inference, KV cache enabled). A CU is used solely for measuring Reserved Capacity and monthly consumption; actual physical assignment may be run on a compatible GPU family.

2) "Baseline Throughput" - means the aggregate model generation throughput measured as tokens per second at P95 latency for the models identified in Appendix A, using a 4,096 token context window and Redwood's standard prompt-template for throughput benchmarking. Baseline throughput per CU is subject to periodic recalibration and mutually agreed updates.

3) "Service Credits" - where Redwood fails to meet the Monthly Availability target as set forth in Appendix A, Customer may be eligible for service credits applied to the monthly Dedicated fees. Credits will be calculated as (Monthly Dedicated Fee) x (Downtime / Monthly Minutes) x Credit Multiplier, with an overall cap equal to fifty percent (50%) of the Monthly Dedicated Fee for the affected month. Credits are the sole and exclusive remedy for availability failures.

4) "Burst Capacity & Overage" - Customers may burst up to 20% of their reserved monthly CUs at published on-demand rates. Overage usage beyond burst thresholds is billed at the on-demand per-CU rate and does not retroactively change discount tiers for prior months; discount tiers are evaluated on the committed monthly reservation amount.

Ask: legal POV on the A100 baseline phrasing and credit cap number. Ops to confirm the 4k context benchmarking and whether the 20% burst is operationally safe. Marcus, can you confirm the billing mechanic for burst and whether we should include a queued preemption statement?

Thanks,
Jordan

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>, neha.kapoor@redwood.com, marcus.lin@redwood.com
Date: Thu, 16 Sep 2026 14:20:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Fwd: HealthBridge questions - draft redlines for Capacity Unit + SLA wording

Jordan, quick edits/suggestions from product/ops:

- CU definition: fine to use GPU-equivalent hour language, but suggest removing specific vendor model in the definition. Replace "NVIDIA Ampere A100-80GB baseline" with "Redwood's defined GPU-equivalent baseline (documented in Appendix A)". We don't want to hardlock to a hardware SKU in the contract.

- Baseline throughput: propose we state a conservative baseline in the contract and keep the detailed benchmarks in Appendix A (e.g., "Baseline throughput per CU: 120 tokens/sec (p95) for 4k context for the qualified model family"). Appendix A can include per-model numbers and test harness links.

- Service credits: suggest formula: Credit = (Monthly Dedicated Fee) x (Percent Minutes Unavailable) x 1.0, cap at 40% of Monthly Dedicated Fee. Also add that credits are exclusive remedy and do not apply to degradation caused by customer config or third-party integrations.

- Overage/discount interaction: confirm that committed CU level determines discount tier for billing period; overages are billed at on-demand and don't reduce the committed bill. Add an option for annual true-up if they want committed spend to be aggregated annually rather than monthly.

I've attached RBW-Dedicated-Pricing-Redline-v1.docx with suggested tracked edits. From an ops perspective, the 20% burst is okay if we reserve a preemption policy: bursts are preemptible if capacity constraints occur and will be throttled based on priority.

-Karthik
Head of Product Operations

From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
To: Elena Torres <elena.torres@healthbridge.com>, procurement@healthbridge.com

Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity commit - clarification on Capacity Units, discounts & SLA redlines

Elena — thanks for the quick turn and great questions. Below are consolidated answers and the redline snippets you can propose to your counsel. If Mike or your internal counsel wants minor edits we can iterate quickly.

1) Capacity Unit (redline):
"Capacity Unit (CU) means one (1) GPU-equivalent hour measured against Redwood's defined GPU-equivalent baseline as documented in Appendix A. Appendix A lists the performance-equivalent hardware and the benchmarking harness used to translate physical GPUs to Capacity Units. A CU is a billing and reservation construct and does not guarantee allocation to a specific physical GPU model.

2) Baseline Throughput (redline):
"Baseline Throughput means tokens-per-second at P95 latency for the model family referenced in Appendix A using a 4,096 token context. For contract purposes, Baseline Throughput per CU shall be 120 tokens/sec at P95 for the baseline model family; Appendix A contains model-by-model throughput tables and test harness links. Redwood will notify Customer at least 60 days prior to any material change to benchmark methodology.

3) Service Credits (redline):
"If Redwood fails to meet the Monthly Availability target set forth in Appendix A, Customer may be eligible for service credits as follows: Credit = (Monthly Dedicated Fee) x (Percent Minutes Unavailable during the billing month). Credits shall not exceed forty percent (40%) of the Monthly Dedicated Fee for the affected month and shall be Customer's sole and exclusive remedy for unavailability. Credits will not apply to outages caused by Customer actions, Force Majeure, or third-party services outside Redwood's control.

4) Burst & Overage (redline):
"Customer may burst above their reserved monthly CUs up to twenty percent (20%) at Redwood's published on-demand per-CU rate. Burst capacity is preemptible under capacity constraints and may be throttled in accordance with Redwood's published priority policies. Overage charges do not retroactively change discount tiers for past billing periods; discount tiers are applied based on the committed reservation in effect for the month. Annual true-up options may be included by mutual written agreement.

Attachments: RBW-Dedicated-Pricing-Redline-v1.docx (redline of Appendix A and pricing table)

Proposed next step: 30-minute call Monday 9/20 or Tue 9/21 to walk Elena, procurement, and Mike through the redline and lock the commit tier + term. If that works I will also include a DocuSign link for the SOW.

Thanks,
Jordan Blake
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
